record.title: The Handler
record.premise: In Helstrom the order's handler hears what the player found, has them win a jar of stolen sap off an Unbound go-between, makes them a Voh-Vastei and sends them after an "Eye of Argonia" for sale in Gideon.
sources: story/design/quests/lines/main-plot.md §3 §4 §5 quest 5 and the rank table §9
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 5 and the rank table. The player rides the rootworm from Jal-Veesa's pool (the travel network's fare line, 25 gold) to Helstrom's city tree, where Cheeval-Xu works the rootworm, and finds Nesh-Deeka's House, one of the city's one-room Argonian houses, its door showing her name. Nesh-Deeka hears the report and tells the player what the Eye of Argonia is and where it lies; the player says what the draught must be for and she agrees. To prove the player she sends them for a jar of stolen sap carried by Keel-Raa, an Unbound go-between who lodges at the Boatmen's Lodge (Helstrom's inn, a ship's hold interior kept by Sleeps-Last) with two hired men beside him, none hostile, in a band of ours whose members' wrongs Helstrom's levy does not punish (Skyrim's flag that reports no crimes against its members). The player lifts the jar from his pack (Pickpocket), buys it for 100 gold, or fights the three for it. On the jar's hand-in Nesh-Deeka makes the player a Voh-Vastei (the rank, Sign of Cipactli's light Argonian armour under our name, the order's traders and 200 gold), gives the order's aim and her one lead, an "Eye of Argonia" for sale in Gideon, by the rootworm from Helstrom's city tree: stage 90, which starts MN06. The rank is given at the end, after the test (the rank table: "given after quest 5").

topics.label: Where is Nesh-Deeka's House?
topics.intent: Cheeval-Xu, at the root landing under the city tree. Tells: he works the rootworm here. Nesh-Deeka's House is a quiet house off the market, one of the houses nearest the city tree; her name is on the door; she takes visitors by word of mouth. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: the Toh-Reel-Ka's handler at Helstrom: she takes the reports of the order's people in this country and gives them their work. Vosh-Leera sends her word now and then. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Vosh-Leera sent me. The Unbound are draining the trees.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: she knows; she hears the player out: the sealed scar, the hide, the camp, Sesk's names. "The Eye" is the Eye of Argonia, the lost jewel of the old priest-kings, who ruled the marsh before any history was written; they cut it from Hist amber, the solid sap the trees no longer make. It lies at the Root, the place under the sea where the roots of every Hist meet, behind a gate that the last king sealed, in a place no living diver has found. Cuts-the-Old-Knot wants it. She asks what the player thinks the draught is for (a question; its answer is topic.mn05-draught). Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Sap makes a fighter strong. Something must guard the Root, and she means to kill it.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: (after topic.mn05-report: the Eye of Argonia is the priest-kings' jewel of Hist amber, at the Root under the sea behind a sealed gate) she agrees: whatever guards the Root, Cuts-the-Old-Knot means to kill it. Now she wants proof of the player. Keel-Raa, an Unbound go-between, lodges at the Boatmen's Lodge, the inn by the city landing, with two hired men and a jar of stolen sap in his pack. Bring her the jar. He is not looking for a fight and will talk, so lift it from his pack, buy it, or take it by force: his band pays the levy to look away from them, so the levy will not count it a crime either. Does: sets stage 20. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about the Eye of Argonia.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: the priest-kings cut it from Hist amber in the oldest days, when the trees still made sap hard as stone. It is said to be the knot that joins every root to every other; used where it sits, it can pour strength down every root. Relic-hunters have chased it for centuries; most chase glass. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the Root?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: every Hist is joined to every other at the root. Under the sea, somewhere off the coast, the roots of every tree meet in one place: the Root. The priest-kings built over it, and the last of them sealed its gate. Nobody living knows the way down. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me the order's history.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: Toh-Reel-Ka is Jel for Secret Warriors. The Xeech-Leel made the order in the Void Nights, 4E 98 to 100, when the moons vanished and the province feared its trees were turning again, as the sworn guard of the Root Talk, the great gathering of the tribes at Helstrom, and of Lilmoth's third tree. Its one charge has not changed: no tree, and no person or group allied with a tree, may bring another Umbriel. It answers to the council of the Xeech-Leel and to nobody else. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What are the order's ranks?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: lowest first, Voh-Vastei, "Apprentice"; Toh-Wo, "Secret-Speaker", one who brings secrets in; Reel-Ka, "Warrior", a full member; Ka-Deelith, "War-Teacher", who trains the warriors; and Toh-Nassa, "Leader of the Secret". Each rank brings gear and gold, and the order's doors open wider. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Xeech-Leel?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: the party that rules the province, the People of the New Beginning; their council sits here in Helstrom, a few streets from her door. They swore to govern in the open. She says it without a smile. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells, in a line or two: the flying city the An-Xileel called down through Lilmoth's mad tree; the order exists so that it never happens again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Keel-Raa. Tells: he carries goods between people who want them, and he lodges here at the Boatmen's Lodge till a buyer comes. Varus and Ah-Meesei are his hired help. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I hear you have a jar of sap.
topics.intent: Keel-Raa. Tells: he does, in his pack, and it stays there until someone pays. A hundred gold, and it is the player's. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: A hundred gold for the jar. (100 gold)
topics.intent: Keel-Raa. Checks: goldAtLeast 100. Tells: a pleasure; he hands over the jar. Does: sets stage 26, whose start takes a hundred gold and gives the jar. Fallback when the check fails: no coin, no jar; he names a hundred again.
topics.fallback: No coin, no jar. A hundred, and it's yours.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Varus Atrius. Tells: hired to stand beside Keel-Raa and look large; he does. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Ah-Meesei. Tells: she guards Keel-Raa's back for coin; the player should keep their hands where she can see them. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Here is Keel-Raa's jar.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Checks: hasItem the jar. Tells: good. She makes the player a Voh-Vastei, an apprentice of the order, and gives them the order's light armour and two hundred gold for the road; the order's traders will deal with them now. The order's aim: the Root must be found before the Unbound find it, and the player is to use the Eye where it sits to heal the trees. She has one lead: an "Eye of Argonia" is for sale in Gideon's market, the relic-dealers' city to the west. Most such eyes are glass; find out where this one came from. The rootworm runs from Helstrom's city tree to Gideon; Cheeval-Xu calls it there. Does: sets stage 90.

topics.label: Remind me what we are hunting, and why.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka, from the player's rank to the end of the line wherever she stands (later lanes add their own rows). Tells: the Hist trees are sickening one by one. The Unbound drain them and seal the scars with a grey paste. Their leader, Cuts-the-Old-Knot, brews the sap into a draught strong enough to kill the beast that guards the Root, the place under the sea where the roots of all the trees meet. There the Eye of Argonia lies, the old priest-kings' jewel of Hist amber, behind a gate the last king sealed. The order wants the player to find it first and use it where it sits to heal the trees. Her one lead now is the "Eye of Argonia" for sale in Gideon. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about Gideon.
topics.intent: Nesh-Deeka. Tells: the relic-dealers' city on the western frontier, full of Imperials and old records; it keeps the Xeech-Leel at arm's length. Its market sells anything said to be old. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

record.premise: A stranger sent up the river on an Owing barge gives the gang's cook their name and trade in the barge's hold, and is freed on the landing by a sour gang-master on an order from Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 1 (passed by the owner, 2026-11-17) and §1. The game opens in the hold of the Owing barge moored at Ashgate Landing; the hold's door is locked. Okeeh, the gang's cook, asks the player's name (the "player's name set from a conversation" block: the stage after her line opens the game's own name entry) and their trade (a profession as in Morrowind: each answer sets a stage that raises five skills by five; one answer lets the player name their own five, one at a time, each pick a stage that raises that skill by five). When the trade is given the door is unlocked from outside. Dralin Uveran, the gang-master, speaks first on the landing (the quest's one speaks-first line), says the player's name was struck from his roll this morning on Vosh-Leera's order, and sends them to her house in Jal-Veesa, passing on the tree-minder's request for Sithis' beard from Reed-Sill Weir on the way. The player's pack holds two lockpicks. MN02 starts on this quest's stage 90 and carries the markers on the weir's moss and on Vosh-Leera's door. The side quest What the Herald Sent is left out: the main quest only. Okeeh and Dralin first answer the line's shared topics Hist, Jal-Veesa and the Owing.

topics.intent: Okeeh. Tells: "You're in the hold of the work barge, moored at Ashgate Landing, a reed-cutters' camp on the river west of Loriasel. This is Black Marsh, the Argonians' country." The barge brought this gang up from the sea to serve the Owing: months of owed work given by the marsh in place of a cell, served here cutting reed for the mat-makers of Stormhold. She is Okeeh, the gang's cook. The door is locked from outside, as it is for every new gang, until the gang-master, a Dunmer named Dralin Uveran, takes their names onto his roll; it will not be long. topics.intent: Okeeh, an Argonian. Tells: a Hist is one of the great trees of Black Marsh, and they think. A Hist is as tall as a tower, with pale grey bark and roots standing up out of the water, and a pool at its foot where the eggs lie among the roots. Every Argonian village is built round its own tree. On a hatchling's naming day it licks its tree's sap, and the sap shapes it for life; her own tree is far to the south, and she still dreams of it. All the trees are joined at the root, so what one knows the others can know. An Argonian with a hand on the bark can hear them. They are not just trees: if a village's tree dies, no egg in its pools will hatch again. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

record.title: The Dry Tree
record.premise: On the road to Jal-Veesa the freed stranger picks Sithis' beard from under the crocodiles at Reed-Sill Weir for the town's sick Hist, and Vosh-Leera tells them that they now work for the Toh-Reel-Ka.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 2 and §2. Starts as MN01 ends, with the player freed and sent to Vosh-Leera. The player picks Sithis' beard below Reed-Sill Weir, past or through two young crocodiles (fight, shoot from the log walk, or sneak), and brings it to Weeltul, Jal-Veesa's tree-minder, at the Hist pool. She shows the sick tree (dry dark bark, a closed scar, a cooling egg-pool), makes a poultice that warms the pool but does not open the scar, says what the town loses if the tree dies, and has the player lay a hand on the bark for the tree's blessing (the town's own shrine-blessing: waterbreathing, or resist poison for an Argonian). Vosh-Leera then tells the player who they now work for, how the An-Xileel used Lilmoth's mad tree to call Umbriel down, and why a stranger with no kin was chosen; she pays 50 gold and asks the player back to her house for a second task, which starts MN03. The jal-veesa-minder of the line is named Weeltul here.

truth.what: Jal-Veesa's Hist fell sick. Its bark dried and darkened, its scar closed and gives no sap, and its egg-pool has cooled. Weeltul cannot find a cause. Sithis' beard, laid in the pool as a poultice, warms the water for a while.

Vosh-Leera, root-herald of the town, began to pass what she heard to a Toh-Reel-Ka handler, without asking what was done with it. This season the order told her to find a stranger with no kin in the work gangs and free them, since such a stranger makes a cheap and useful spy; she chose the player from the barge's list.

The An-Xileel, who then ruled Black Marsh, used Lilmoth's mad Hist to call the flying city Umbriel down on the marsh; its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The An-Xileel fell. The Xeech-Leel rose by being their opposite, and in 4E 98 to 100 made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree and nobody allied with a tree could do it again.

topics.intent: Weeltul. Checks: hasItem [thing.mn02.sithis-beard, 1]. Tells: she takes it and lays it in the pool as a poultice. She shows the player the tree: its bark should be pale grey and soft and is dry and dark; its scar, the one place in the bark where she draws a little sap, has closed and gives nothing; its egg-pool, where the town's eggs lie among the roots, is cooling. topics.label: Tell me about the eggs.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: Argonian eggs are laid in the pool among a Hist's roots, and the tree keeps them warm and alive through its roots. If a tree's bond with its eggs is cut, the unborn die in the shell. A village whose tree dies has no future: nothing in its pools will hatch again. This pool is cooling; she has turned the eggs twice today. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the sap?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: sap is what a Hist bleeds, amber-coloured and thick. A hatchling licks its tree's sap on its naming day, and the sap shapes its body for life. Drunk, it brings visions the tree sends, of far places; minders drink a little to ask the trees a question. It makes a fighter stronger for a time, which is why some steal it. In the old days the trees made it hard as stone, amber, but no tree does that now. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the scar?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: every Hist has one place in its bark, low on the trunk, where its minder cuts a little and the tree gives sap there and nowhere else; that is the scar. A healthy tree's scar weeps sap when it is opened. A sick tree's scar closes over and gives nothing. Jal-Veesa's closed this season. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Why did you have me freed?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera, in her house, privately: nobody names the order aloud in company. Tells: the player has seen the tree. Trees are falling sick, one at a time, along the river, and nobody knows why. The people she answers to want it found. They are the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors: the elite order of the Xeech-Leel, the People of the New Beginning, who have ruled the province since the An-Xileel fell. In 4E 48 the An-Xileel, who ruled then, used the mad Hist of Lilmoth to call down the flying city Umbriel, and its dead killed Lilmoth's people. The Xeech-Leel made the Toh-Reel-Ka so that no tree, and nobody allied with a tree, can ever turn on the marsh like that again. They comb the work gangs for strangers with no kin and no ties, because such a stranger makes a useful spy and a cheap one; she chose the player off the barge's list. Nobody in the marsh is owed a reason. They pay, and they give work. She gives the player fifty gold and asks them to come back to her, here, for a second task. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Tell me about the Toh-Reel-Ka.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Toh-Reel-Ka is Jel for "Secret Warriors": toh, secret, as in xal-toh, sacred secret, and reel-ka, warrior. They are the Xeech-Leel's order of spies and guards, made in the Void Nights, when the moons vanished and the province feared its trees were turning again. They watch the trees and anyone who seeks a tree's power, and they answer only to the Xeech-Leel's council at Helstrom. They wear no mark; their handlers keep quiet houses in the cities; people like her pass on what they hear. She has never asked what they do with it. Nobody names them aloud in company, and neither should the player. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Xeech-Leel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: Xeech-Leel means the People of the New Beginning: Xeech, the planting month, and leel, people. They took the province in the generations after Umbriel by being everything the An-Xileel were not. Their first promise is that no faction may speak alone with a tree; they swore to govern in the open, and their council sits at Helstrom. They hold the old forts, roads and tolls through their Archwardens; inland the towns and tribes run themselves, as Jal-Veesa does. People call them "the Wardens", or "the New Beginning". Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What was Umbriel?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. record.premise: Vosh-Leera's cup of sap shows the player a young Hist and a reed hide; at Teel-Fen Weir they find the young tree's scar sealed with a grey paste, take a jar and a note from the hide's sap-takers, and tell the tree's minder the truth or a comfort.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 3. Vosh-Leera gives the player a cup of sap (Skyrim's potion bottle under our name); the player drinks it in front of her by a line. The stage it sets fades the screen to black and shows the vision's words on a message box while it is black (the approved fade-with-message block); the player then tells it to her line by line, and she names Teel-Fen Weir, south of the town, whose young Hist grew from Jal-Veesa's roots. Heem-Jasa shows the grey paste in the young tree's closed scar and points to the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir, where three Unbound sap-takers keep jars of sap. The player fights them, shoots them from cover or passes them by stealth to take the note (taking it moves the quest; a jar lies beside it to take as well). Back on the platform Heem-Jasa asks whether her tree will live: the truth opens her Alchemy training (Adept) and her stall; a comfort gives three potions of Cure Poison on the spot and leaves her training and stall closed. The note orders the crew to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp, which starts MN04.

record.premise: At the Naga camp where the sap goes, the player frees Sesk from her cage and hears the names of the Unbound and Cuts-the-Old-Knot; Vosh-Leera sends them by the rootworm to the order's handler in Helstrom.
record.foundation: Built from main-plot.md §5 quest 4. Starts on any of MN03's complete endings (90, 91, 92), all of which leave the player holding the note that names Karsh-Naal Camp; this quest's first stage marks the camp on the map. Sesk is caged at the camp's edge (Skyrim's cage door, placed, Novice lock); its key is on Jeeta-Sakka, the guard who stands at the fire with three others, away from the cage. The player picks the cage, lifts the key or kills the guards; opening the cage door (a use hook) moves the quest. Sesk names the Unbound and Cuts-the-Old-Knot, says the sap is for a draught that has something to do with "the Eye", and calls the grey paste "the seal". Back in Jal-Veesa Vosh-Leera sends the player to the order's handler in Helstrom and pays 100 gold; Weeltul, at the Hist pool, explains the rootworm and its 25-gold fare, and the quest ends there; MN05 carries the ride and the handler's house.

topics.label: Who's in the cage?
topics.intent: Sesk, through the bars. Tells: she is Sesk, and she will tell the player everything about the sap if they get her out. The key is on Jeeta-Sakka, the big one at the fire; the lock is a poor one; the guards never look this way. Her sack is on the floor in there with her; when the door is open, the player is to hand it to her. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who are you?
topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: a Naga: the Naga are tribeless Argonians of the deep marsh, tall and hard, who sell their blades or their hands to whoever pays. She drew sap for the Unbound and tried to leave with her pay. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Here is your sack. Tell me about the sap.
topics.intent: Sesk, out of the cage. Tells: the crews who drain the trees are the Unbound, a cult of the tribeless, and their leader is Cuts-the-Old-Knot. Sesk drew sap for them: cut the scar, fill the jars, press the grey paste in after. They call the paste "the seal"; she never knew what is in it, and she was told never to leave a scar open. The jars come here and go on to Cuts-the-Old-Knot. The sap is for a draught she brews, and the draught is for something to do with "the Eye"; Sesk never learned what. She wants out, with the price of a boat, and goes now, before the guards look round. Does: sets stage 30. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Who are the Unbound?
topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: tribeless people, Argonians with no tree or kin that will have them, and a few others, who follow Cuts-the-Old-Knot. They pay well in coin and say they will set the marsh free; she never learned free of what. They move in small crews and meet nowhere twice. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Who is Cuts-the-Old-Knot?
topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: the Unbound's leader. Sesk saw her once: an Argonian woman, thin, quiet, who looked at the trees as if they had wronged her. She never stays where her crews are. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: What is the seal?
topics.intent: Sesk. Tells: the grey paste the crews press into a scar after they drain it; the cut closes over it. It comes in bottles from Cuts-the-Old-Knot's people. Sesk does not know what is in it or why they use it. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: I found where the sap goes.
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: she hears it all: the Unbound, Cuts-the-Old-Knot, a draught, "the Eye", the seal. This is more than a herald can judge. The order's handler for this country is Nesh-Deeka, who keeps a quiet house in Helstrom, the oldest city, far to the south, where the Xeech-Leel's council sits; the door bears her name. The road there runs through deadly country, so the player is to ride the rootworm: Weeltul calls it at the Hist pool in the middle of the town, and the fare is twenty-five gold. She pays the player a hundred gold. Does: sets stage 40, whose start gives the gold. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: Who is Nesh-Deeka?
topics.intent: Vosh-Leera. Tells: a handler is the one who takes the order's reports in a city and gives its work. Nesh-Deeka is the handler at Helstrom; Vosh-Leera has met her twice and found her sharp and well informed. Helstrom is the oldest city of the Argonians, at the river fork in the middle of the Hist forest, a city no invader ever took. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.

topics.label: Vosh-Leera says you can send me to Helstrom by the rootworm.
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: the rootworm is a great worm, longer than a boat, that swims through the waters under the roots between the trees' pools; a tree-minder calls it, and a rider holds on in its mouth-hollow and comes up in another tree's pool. From this pool it goes to Helstrom's city tree. The fare is twenty-five gold, paid to her when the player is ready to go: ask her to call it. In Helstrom, the house of anyone the player wants will be off the market; the city's rootworm caller can point the way. Does: sets stage 90. Checks: nothing.

topics.label: What is the rootworm?
topics.intent: Weeltul. Tells: a worm of the deep roots, blind and patient, older than the town. It follows the roots from tree to tree under the water and mud, faster than any boat. Tree-minders call it with a hand on the bark. It carries a rider who keeps still and holds their breath for a little; it does not bite those the tree knows. It runs from here to Helstrom. Checks: nothing. Does: nothing.
